packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Disclosures
- Nothing in my context gave a proposed identification or reading of this text before I read the images. Some phrases looked familiar while I was reading. I did not use memory to fill gaps. Every gap below is a gap in what I could see.
- Beyond the instructions: I ran `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames. I did not open packet.json or any other directory.
- All 26 images loaded. None failed.

Image map (from the layout)
- image-001: overview of face 1 (pencil shelfmark at foot "Stams, STA, Frg. 214_1r"; blue pencil "Einband von IVa/F2").
- image-002..013: native tiles of face 1. Rows run top to bottom and each row is left, middle, right: 002/003/004, 005/006/007, 008/009/010, 011/012/013.
- image-014: overview of face 2 (pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 214_1v").
- image-015..026: native tiles of face 2 in the same pattern: 015/016/017, 018/019/020, 021/022/023, 024/025/026.
- Both overviews show three loose narrow strips of the same script beside the leaf. No native tiles of the strips were supplied (see Limitations).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- One parchment leaf, upright, two columns, about 28 ruled lines per column, Gothic textualis. The folded margins show it was reused as a binding.
- Face 1: red rubrics inside the columns ("...li · Sapiẽtie", "Sapien-", "Ep(isto)la", "Ad Ephesios"). Large red initial H in column b, top. Blue initial B with red penwork in column b, lower. Red touches on capitals (Q, D, C, G, E, S). A large hole and torn area cross the middle of column a and the left of column b. A paper label is pasted over column b mid-height, in a later cursive hand: "Triumphus B. / Mariae / Disputationes / variae philosoph[...]" (my reading, uncertain). Small brownish "F"-like marks sit in the intercolumn space beside column a, lower half (image-009). Their purpose is unclear.
- Face 2: a red number or folio mark sits above column b (image-016): "cc xvij"? (uncertain). Short red rubrics inside column a ("Ser'"/"Secr'"?, "Cplı̄"/"Co(m)pl(e)n(da)"?, "Alia collecta", "ut sup(ra)", "aplor(um) · Or(ati)o", "Ad Ephesios"). Alternating blue and red initials in column a. Column b has a large red initial F at the top, a large blue initial (F-shaped?) at mid-column, and the red rubric "Ad Romanos ·". The surface is badly abraded, with white patches of paper/paste residue in vertical bands. Tiny printed-looking paper scraps adhere at image-019 ("e / ·vu") and image-017 ("w"), with a paper patch at image-025.
- Tentative interpretation, not an identification: the short red headings (Secr., Compl., Alia collecta, Or(ati)o, Ep(isto)la, Lectio) and the alternation of prayer texts with lections look like a liturgical book. There is no gloss or commentary layer. All text is main text plus rubrics.

SELECTED SPANS
Read: both columns of both faces wherever ink survives, including most of the connected prose. Left largely unread: the torn and holed band in mid-column a and the left of column b on face 1 (image-008/009), the matching band in column b of face 2 (image-019/022/023), and the loose strips.

Conventions: (..) = proposed expansion; ? = uncertain reading (placed after the word); [..] = traces too faint to read; [illegible] = unreadable; [red] = rubricated. Line numbers count from the top of the cited image. Tiles overlap, so a line seen on two tiles is given once, with both tiles cited.

LIMITATIONS
- The mid-leaf hole and shrivelled strips on both faces remove about 5-6 lines in column a of face 1 and about 4-5 lines in column b of face 2. Those lines are effectively unread.
- Face 2 has heavy abrasion and white residue. Many word-middles in column a there are uncertain.
- On face 1 the paper label hides the left half of about 4 lines in column b.
- The order of the two faces (1r/1v) is taken only from the pencil shelfmarks. I have not checked it from the text.
- Abbreviations are expanded tentatively. "neqz" means the q-with-3 form for neque.

SUGGESTED FURTHER IMAGES
- Native-resolution crops of the three loose strips, both sides.
- Raking or UV light on the abraded band in face 2, column a, and on the faded line above "Ad Ephesios" on face 1 (010.4-5).
- If possible, a view under or behind the pasted label on face 1, column b.
